Donor offset-pseudobulk negative-binomial sc-ExWAS

Source: R/glmm-inference.R
run_sc_exwas_pb_offset.Rd

A donor-level negative-binomial alternative to run_sc_exwas. Per cell type and per gene, aggregates cells to a donor pseudobulk count and fits a negative-binomial GLM with a library-size offset \(\log s_i = \log(\text{donor total counts})\). Lee and Han (2024) report that pseudobulk models with proper offsets have the same statistical properties as generalised linear mixed models in single-cell case-control studies, without the pseudoreplication that inflates cell-level tests. P-values are Wald tests with an estimated dispersion and can be anticonservative when there are few donors. The function has no threshold on the number of cells: every donor with at least one cell of a cell type enters the model of that cell type, where run_sc_exwas leaves out a donor with fewer than min_cells cells.

Usage

run_sc_exwas_pb_offset(
  x,
  exposure,
  celltype_col = "cell_type",
  covariates = NULL,
  target_genes = NULL,
  BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()
)

Arguments

x

A SingleCellExposomeExperiment. Each cell's donor is read from the colData column named by sampleColumn(x).

exposure

Character; a donor-level column of exposureData(x).

celltype_col

Character. Column in colData containing cell type annotations. Default "cell_type".

covariates

Character vector; donor covariate columns in exposureData (numeric), added as GLM main effects. The names y, A and logoff are used by the model and cannot be covariate names, and each name must be a syntactic R name (see make.names) other than ., ... and names such as ..1, which R reads specially in a formula. The exposure itself cannot be a covariate.

target_genes

Character; genes to test (default: all rows of x).

BPPARAM

A BiocParallel param used to parallelise over genes. Defaults to BiocParallel::SerialParam(), so no worker process is started unless one is asked for; pass, for example, BiocParallel::SnowParam(workers = 2L) to fit genes in parallel. Pass NULL to use a plain lapply.

Value

A DataFrame, one row per gene x cell type: gene, celltype, log2FC (exposure effect on the \(\log_2\) rate scale), se (on the same scale), statistic (donor-level Wald z from the NB GLM), pvalue, and padj_global (BH across all tested gene-by-cell-type strata, as in run_sc_exwas; there is no within-cell-type padj). Rows ordered by padj_global, then pvalue. A gene whose GLM cannot be fitted gets NA estimates; the function stops when no cell type has at least three donors with cells.

Note

Report empirical calibration from a donor-permutation null, with the exposure permuted across donors, before quoting any type-I rate.

References

Lee H & Han B (2024). Pseudobulk with proper offsets has the same statistical properties as generalized linear mixed models in single-cell case-control studies. Bioinformatics 40(8):btae498. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btae498

Squair JW et al. (2021). Confronting false discoveries in single-cell differential expression. Nat Commun 12:5692.

See also

run_sc_exwas_glmm for the cell-level LMM reference.

Examples

donor_ids <- paste0("D", seq_len(10L))
exposure <- rep(c(0, 1), each = 5L)
cell_donor <- rep(donor_ids, each = 10L)
cell_type <- rep("TypeA", length(cell_donor))
cell_ids <- paste0("cell", seq_along(cell_donor))
pb_targets <- rbind(
    G1 = c(30, 140, 50, 180, 40, 110, 260, 70, 220, 130),
    G2 = c(200, 40, 240, 60, 300, 50, 270, 80, 330, 70),
    G3 = c(100, 120, 90, 150, 110, 130, 170, 100, 160, 140),
    G4 = c(250, 200, 300, 180, 270, 220, 320, 210, 290, 230)
)
counts <- matrix(0L, nrow = 4L, ncol = length(cell_ids))
for (donor in seq_along(donor_ids)) {
    counts[, cell_donor == donor_ids[donor]] <- pb_targets[, donor] / 10L
}
storage.mode(counts) <- "integer"
dimnames(counts) <- list(paste0("G", seq_len(4L)), cell_ids)
sce <- SingleCellExperiment::SingleCellExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = counts),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        cell_id = cell_ids,
        donor_id = cell_donor,
        cell_type = cell_type
    )
)
donor_design <- matrix(exposure, ncol = 1L,
    dimnames = list(donor_ids, "exposure"))
scee <- build_scee(sce, donor_design, sample_col = "donor_id")
offset_result <- run_sc_exwas_pb_offset(
    scee,
    exposure = "exposure",
    celltype_col = "cell_type",
    target_genes = c("G1", "G2"),
    BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()
)
head(offset_result)
#> DataFrame with 2 rows and 7 columns
#>          gene    celltype    log2FC        se statistic    pvalue padj_global
#>   <character> <character> <numeric> <numeric> <numeric> <numeric>   <numeric>
#> 1          G1       TypeA  0.468350  0.507553  0.922762  0.356131    0.426691
#> 2          G2       TypeA -0.390771  0.491618 -0.794867  0.426691    0.426691
